summary: Shoshone NF stone-and-rock fire lookout in the Wind River Range, built by the CCC in 1938 and NHLR-registered in 1998; sources disagree on whether the structure still stands.

facts.design: open rock structure with fire finder, flag, and stone wall, reached by stone stairs
facts.status_note: Sources disagree: firelookout.com says Gone; the Association's Wyoming list says Stone Walls, Abandoned; no source describes the present condition

access.note: A family blog describes a one-mile round-trip hike to the lookout; the Forest Service is not cited for access and no closure is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About one mile round trip from a trailhead on the Sinks Canyon-Louis Lake Road, about 23 miles southwest of Lander (per a family blog); check current conditions with the Shoshone National Forest

events.note: Built by the CCC; the groundhouse, now the Louis Lake Guard Station, was also CCC-built
Registered August 22, 1998 as US 255, WY 6; nominated by Burns Davison, district ranger, Washakie RD

evidence.quote: The Blue Ridge Lookout was constructed in 1938.

corrections.why: firelookout.com says Gone, but the Association's own Wyoming list says Stone Walls, Abandoned, and the NHLR describes the structure in detail with 2013 photographs. No source settles the present condition, so 'gone' is contested rather than established.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says Gone; firelookout.org lists Stone Walls, Abandoned. Not resolved by the sources read.
firelookout.com gives 18 miles southwest of Lander; the family blog gives about 23 miles to the trailhead. The two may measure different points; not confirmed.

sources.title: Blue Ridge Lookout: A Perfect Family Hike

notes_for_editor: Key open question is current condition: the sources conflict and none is recent. Access rests on one family blog of unknown date; verify with the Shoshone National Forest before publishing access wording. Brief record 'gone' is contested. Blog quote about 23 miles is for the trailhead, firelookout.com's 18 miles for the lookout (unconfirmed).
